_comment: Golden vectors for PROTOCOL §4.2 / ADR-015. Rule: the surviving connection is the one initiated by the peer with the LARGER conn_tiebreak. Leadership (ADR-010) is a separate, uncorrelated computation over peer_id — see ADR-015 Amendment A2 and ADR-010 Amendment A2, corrected this session: no implementation may assume initiator==leader or acceptor==leader.

vectors.name: larger-tiebreak-outbound-survives
vectors.note: peer_a's conn_tiebreak is lexicographically larger, so peer_a's outbound (initiated) connection is the survivor

vectors.name: smaller-tiebreak-outbound-loses
vectors.note: same data as larger-tiebreak-outbound-survives, restated from the losing side: peer_b's outbound connection is closed and this is neither a fault nor a state transition (ARCHITECTURE §3 rule 6)

vectors.name: both-peers-derive-same-verdict
vectors.note: both sides observe the same pair of conn_tiebreak values and must reach the same verdict with no extra round trip

vectors.name: equal-tiebreak-both-close-and-regenerate
vectors.note: probability 2^-128 in practice; both sides must independently detect the tie identically

vectors.name: initiator-not-assumed-leader
vectors.note: peer_a initiates the surviving connection (larger conn_tiebreak) but peer_b leads (smaller peer_id, ADR-010) — proves initiator != leader is a legal, expected outcome

vectors.name: acceptor-not-assumed-leader
vectors.note: peer_a again initiates the surviving connection, and this time peer_a ALSO leads (smaller peer_id) — the acceptor (peer_b) is not the leader here either. Read together with initiator-not-assumed-leader, leadership lands on either side of the surviving connection depending only on peer_id, never on who dialled
